chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him), passed by a group of people and greeted them. They said, 'Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings, and His forgiveness, and His pleasure.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them, 'Do not exceed us with more than what the angels said to our father Ibrahim (peace be upon him). They only said, "The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O People of the Household."'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the greeting 'Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs the people to limit their greeting to 'mery and blessings,' mirroring the angels' address to Prophet Ibrahim, thereby distinguishing the Imams' status as recipients of divine grace from Allah as the sole source. This establishes a key Shia theological principle of *tawhid* in attributes, ensuring that while Imams are honored, they are not attributed with divine powers like forgiveness (*maghfira*) or pleasure (*ridwan*) which belong exclusively to God. The narration highlights the precision in liturgical language to maintain the boundary between the Creator and the chosen servants.
